disease_label_per_paper: Relapsed acute myeloid leukemia manifested by gallbladder infiltration presenting as cholecystitis and sepsis
presentation_summary: 50-year-old man with AML history in morphologic free state presented with worsening diarrhea, intermittent nausea/vomiting, fever, right upper quadrant pain, and decreased oral intake after chronic cholecystitis.
Initial labs showed pancytopenia: hemoglobin 98 g/L, platelets 17 x10^9/L, WBC 1.1 x10^9/L with 0% blasts, ALP 218 U/L, and total bilirubin 28 umol/L.

He had cholecystitis and febrile neutropenia treated conservatively with broad-spectrum antibiotics, then recurrent symptoms six days after discharge requiring further antibiotics and cholecystostomy.
CT showed gallbladder distension and thickening consistent with cholecystitis but no peri-cholecystic fluid or inflammatory changes; pathology later showed leukemic gallbladder infiltration.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Gallbladder histopathology showed leukemic infiltration by atypical myeloid cells
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Histopathologic examination demonstrated multiple scattered, highly atypical single cells ... consistent with leukemic infiltration

confirmatory_findings.finding: Immunohistochemistry supported myeloid lineage with CD68, CD33 and CD117 staining
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: abnormal cells demonstrated immunohistochemical staining for CD68, CD33 and CD117

confirmatory_findings.finding: Prior relapse had been confirmed by bone marrow biopsy, peripheral smear, flow cytometry and elevated LDH
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: relapse ... confirmed by bone marrow biopsy (10-12% blasts), peripheral blood smear (5-6% blasts), flow cytometry and an elevated LDH of 638 U/L

actual_treatment: broad-spectrum intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam during febrile neutropenia/cholecystitis admission
vancomycin, colistin, metronidazole, and voriconazole on readmission
percutaneous cholecystostomy tube for source control
outcome: Post-operative recovery was adequate, but relapse precluded bone marrow transplantation
quality_warnings: Gallbladder IHC, tissue pathology, bone marrow biopsy, flow cytometry, and cytogenetic/molecular-style confirmatory tests are kept under confirmatory_findings only.
The diagnostic snapshot uses fever, cytopenias, cholestatic labs, symptoms, antibiotic nonresponse, and source-control context rather than the final tissue diagnosis.
